page.title: Compile, lint, draw and run an order chart
page.description: Compile an order chart, fix a misspelt event with tinyactors lint, find the path to shipped and run one order with tinyactors run.

hero.headline: Compile, lint, draw and run an order chart
hero.lede: In seven commands you take an order chart from a draft with a hidden mistake to an order paid on its second attempt.

section.heading: 1. Compile the order chart
section.p: An order collects items and asks a payment service for a charge. After 30 seconds of silence it asks again, three times at most.
Save it as order.scxml; compile turns it into order.tai, the image your application loads. The chart compiles with no diagnostics.

section.heading: 2. Ask lint what cannot work
section.p: A chart that compiles can still wait for an event that never comes. lint reads the chart without running it.
paying sends itself payment.timeout, but its transitions wait for payment.timedout. An order whose payment service never answers would wait forever.

section.heading: 3. Fix the event and check again
section.p: Change payment.timedout to payment.timeout in both transitions of paying.
check -W compiles the chart, writes nothing, and fails on a warning as on an error.
With --deny all, any finding makes lint exit with 1. It now finds nothing and exits with 0.

section.heading: 4. Find the way to shipped
section.p: path finds the shortest sequence of transitions from open to a state. An order ships after three events, and checkout needs a total above 0.

section.heading: 5. Draw the chart
section.p: graph -f svg draws every state as a box and every transition as a labelled route. The picture follows your system's light or dark setting.

drawing.alt: The order chart: open, paying, paid, shipped and cancelled, with paying's retry looping back to itself

section.heading: 6. Run one order
section.p: tinyactors run reads JSON-RPC requests, one a line. This session adds a pen to an order, checks out, lets 30 seconds pass, then answers the second charge.
--io-processor payments makes your session the payment service. Each effect.send is a charge the order asks of it.
With request 5 the clock moves 30 seconds, so the next turn fires the timeout you fixed. Request 9 reads the order in paid.

section.heading: Put the checks in your build
section.p: In CI, fmt and diff join check and lint to fail a pull request before it merges.

item.text: Run check, lint, fmt and diff on every pull request.
